text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali meets Emir of Bahrain.

- Moslem Brotherhood executive have not taken a decision to boycott parliamentary elections. Leadership of the Brotherhood's political arm, the Islamic Action front, signal they will resign if boycott decision taken. Other opposition parties call for unified election list for opposition.
- U.N. committee approves new export contract for Jordanian medicine to Iraq worth $6.7 million under oil-for-food deal.
- Interior Ministry starts checks into funding and membership of political parties for the first time since they were legalised in 1992.
- Jordan's ambassador to Belgium says the European Union is discussing Spain's opposition to Jordanian tomato paste exports.
- Water Ministry official says water Jordan receives from Sea of Galilee is up to international standards.
- Investors in tourism projects in Jordan face laws and conditions imposed by non-governmental organisations.

- Analysts agree that lifting of foreign ownership ceiling and planned privatisations as well as expected anti-monopoly law all qualify Jordanian market to attract investment and encourage repatriation of Jordanian money from abroad.
- Abolishing limits on foreign ownership of equity poised to attract over $400 million.
